subject: Delivery plan for admin activity evidence shards
thread_summary: Customer requested chunked/shard delivery of admin activity logs with verification checksums and redaction guidance; internal team proposed a per-shard manifest, HMAC verification, and flexible delivery (S3 presigned or SFTP).
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@aegismed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Cc: compliance@aegismed.com
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Delivery plan for admin activity evidence shards

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the run-through on Friday. AegisMed's auditors will want an ingestable package of admin activity (operator events, privilege elevations, session starts/stops) for a rolling 90-day window. Because of the size we're asking whether Redwood can provide the export as chunked "shards" (e.g., daily per-region files) plus a manifest and verification checksum for each shard.

Specific asks from the SIG/SOC2 request:
- Preserve per-event timestamps and actor identity (user id, role) in the export; PII redaction should be limited to user email where requested.
- Provide a signed manifest with per-file SHA256 and an overall HMAC.
- Support both HTTPS presigned URLs and SFTP handoff (we're evaluating constraints with our security team).
- A sample shard (one day, one region) and a manifest would help the auditor run an ingest test.

Attached: SIG_Request_Form.pdf (redacted sample fields). Can you confirm what Redwood logs by default, proposed retention slices, and how you would package the shards? Also note: our security team requires SHA256 + timestamped signature for each shard.

Best,
Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Compliance, AegisMed
Attachment: SIG_Request_Form.pdf (1.2MB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@aegismed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delivery plan for admin activity evidence shards

Tara —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front: yes, we can do shard-based export with per-file SHA256 and an HMAC'd manifest; we can provide either presigned HTTPS URLs or an SFTP drop. I attached a short proposed manifest schema and a CSV-style shard manifest that maps to our export engine.

What we log by default (summary):
- Operator actions: login, logout, role-change, token creation/revocation, CLI/API admin calls (including route, status code)
- Resource-level changes: model deploys, rollout events, config updates
- System events: autoscaler actions and scheduled maintenance markers (tagged)
- Request metadata: request_id, originating IP, user-agent, session id, timestamp (ISO8601)

Retention/packaging proposal:
- Shards = daily, per-region (UTC date + region shard key).
- Compression: gzip per-shard (.jsonl.gz).
- Redaction: we will optionally scrub email addresses and full-name PII; we keep user_id and role.
- Manifest: CSV mapping: shard_filename, start_ts, end_ts, events_count, sha256, shard_size_bytes.
- Signed manifest: we will produce an HMAC-SHA256 over the manifest content and timestamp it; we can also sign with a delegated key if required.

Next steps: 
1) Karthik, Marcus — can you QA the attached sample manifest and confirm we can generate an example shard (one day, us-west-2) by EOD tomorrow?
2) Tara — which delivery method should we prepare first (HTTPS presigned or SFTP)? If you want both, we'll stage presigned links and hold SFTP credentials as fallback.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-shard-manifest.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Tara Singh <tara.singh@aegismed.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delivery plan for admin activity evidence shards

On Mon, Aug 10, 2026 at 11:05 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> Tara —
> 
> Thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front: yes, we can do shard-based export with per-file SHA256 and an HMAC'd manifest; we can provide either presigned HTTPS URLs or an SFTP drop. I attached a short proposed manifest schema and a CSV-style shard manifest that maps to our export engine.

Quick technical notes: 
- We can generate the sample shard as requested. The export pipeline supports event-level JSONL with a stable event_id and an internal sequence number to preserve ordering.
- Checksum plan: compute SHA256 on the compressed file bytes. For the manifest HMAC, we'll use an HMAC-SHA256 keyed by an ephemeral per-delivery key (rotate per-handshake). We will provide the HMAC key fingerprint in the transfer metadata.
- Delivery options:
  * Presigned HTTPS: links expire (configurable). We'll provide a signed manifest file (manifest.csv) and a manifest.signature (HMAC base64).
  * SFTP: we can push to a customer-provided server or accept an SFTP endpoint. For SFTP we will still include a detached signature file and a checksum index (shard-index-example.jsonl attached).
- Verification: auditors typically run sha256sum on the downloaded object and compare with the manifest. We'll include a short verification readme.
- Redaction caveat: if AegisMed wants email redaction, we will replace email fields with a stable surrogate (user_id) and include a mapping only under NDA.

Timeline: sample shard + manifest by Tue EOD (tomorrow PST). Full 90-day rolling export can be staged as incremental daily uploads after acceptance.

Marcus - any infra constraints on producing presigned links for a bulk download (50–100 GB) in a single handoff?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Platform Engineering
Attachment: shard-index-example.jsonl

From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@aegismed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, compliance@aegismed.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delivery plan for admin activity evidence shards

Kimberly, Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turn. Presigned HTTPS links for the sample shard first would be ideal so our auditors can do the ingest test in their sandbox; please set expiry to 72 hours and include the manifest.signature (HMAC base64) alongside. If the sample looks good we'll request the SFTP push for the full 90-day window.

Also please include the following in the sample package: 
- a short verification README with commands (sha256sum, sample verify script)
- the manifest.csv + manifest.signature
- a single-line provenance note (who generated export, job id, timestamp)

We will route the sample to our auditors (AuditOps) and confirm. Once verified we'll provide a DocuSign for the NDA addendum that allows the mapping file with user email to be delivered.

Accepted timeline: sample shard + manifest by Tue EOD -> we'll review Wed morning. If anything slips, loop in Jonas for escalation.

Thanks,
Tara
Attachment: none
